docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A Prometheus exporter that runs speedtest.net measurements and exports the results as metrics.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Periodic speedtest measurements
  • Prometheus metrics for:
  • Ping latency (average, low, high)
  • Download performance (bandwidth, bytes, elapsed time, latency)
  • Upload performance (bandwidth, bytes, elapsed time, latency)
  • Configurable test intervals
  • Multi-architecture support (amd64, arm64, armv7)
  • Docker support
  • Minimal resource footprint (<1MiB RAM usage)

Container memory usage example

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
The fastest way to get started is using our docker-compose file which includes: - Speedtest exporter (running tests every 30 minutes) - Prometheus (pre-configured to scrape the metrics) - Grafana (with auto-provisioned dashboard)

# Download the docker-compose.yml
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lpicanco/prometheus-speedtest-exporter/main/docker-compose.yml

# Start the stack
docker-compose up -d

Then access Grafana at http://localhost:3000 (admin/admin) and you'll find: - Pre-configured Prometheus data source - Auto-provisioned Internet Speed dashboard - Real-time metrics for download, upload, and ping latency

docs.title: Grafana Dashboard
docs.text:
A pre-configured Grafana dashboard is available to visualize your internet speed metrics:

You can import this dashboard in two ways: 1. Using the Grafana.com dashboard ID: 22651 2. Directly from Grafana.com marketplace

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: For detailed documentation, please visit our GitHub repository.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The exporter can be configured using environment variables:

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Default SPEEDTEST_INTERVAL Interval between speedtests in minutes 30 SPEEDTEST_SERVER_ID Specific speedtest.net server ID to use Not set (auto) LISTEN_ADDRESS Address to listen on 0.0.0.0:9516

docs.title: Docker Configuration
docs.text:
When using Docker, you can pass environment variables using the -e flag: 

docker run -p 9516:9516 \
  -e SPEEDTEST_INTERVAL=15 \
  -e SPEEDTEST_SERVER_ID=1234 \
  ghcr.io/lpicanco/prometheus-speedtest-exporter:latest

docs.title: Docker Compose Configuration
docs.text:
In your docker-compose.yml: 

services:
  speedtest-exporter:
    image: ghcr.io/lpicanco/prometheus-speedtest-exporter:latest
    environment:
      - SPEEDTEST_INTERVAL=15
      - SPEEDTEST_SERVER_ID=1234
    ports:
      - "9516:9516"

docs.title: Grafana Dashboard
docs.text: A pre-configured Grafana dashboard is available to visualize your internet speed metrics.

docs.title: Dashboard Features
docs.text: The dashboard includes: - Download and upload speed trends - Ping latency statistics - Jitter measurements - Historical performance graphs - Server information

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The dashboard is available on Grafana.com: Internet Speed Dashboard

You can import it using: - Dashboard ID: 22634 - Direct import from Grafana.com marketplace

docs.title: Docker Compose Setup
docs.text:
If you're using our Docker Compose setup, the dashboard is automatically provisioned and ready to use.

  1. Access Grafana at http://localhost:3000
  2. Login with default credentials (admin/admin)
  3. Navigate to Dashboards -> Internet Speed

docs.title: Manual Setup
docs.text:
If you're setting up the dashboard manually:

  1. Add Prometheus as a data source in Grafana
  2. Import the dashboard using ID 22634
  3. Select your Prometheus data source
  4. Save and enjoy your internet speed metrics!

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Rust and Cargo (latest stable version)
  • Ookla Speedtest CLI version 1.2.0 or higher

docs.title: Build Steps
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/lpicanco/prometheus-speedtest-exporter.git
cd prometheus-speedtest-exporter

# Build in release mode
cargo build --release

# Run tests
cargo test

# Run linting
cargo clippy

docs.title: GitHub Pages Setup
docs.text:
1. Go to your repository's Settings
  2. Navigate to "Pages" under "Code and automation" in the sidebar
  3. Under "Build and deployment":
  4. For "Source", select "Deploy from a branch"
  5. For "Branch", select gh-pages and / (root)
  6. Click "Save"

After configuration, your documentation will be available at https://<username>.github.io/<repository>.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
# Install Python dependencies
pip install mkdocs-material pillow cairosvg

docs.title: Local Development
docs.text:
# Start local server
cd docs
mkdocs serve

Visit http://127.0.0.1:8000 to see the documentation.

docs.title: Building for Production
docs.text:
# Build static site
cd docs
mkdocs build

The built site will be in the site directory at the root of the project.

docs.title: Local Build
docs.text:
# Build the image
docker build -t prometheus-speedtest-exporter .

# Run the container
docker run -p 9516:9516 prometheus-speedtest-exporter

docs.title: Multi-architecture Build
docs.text:
# Set up buildx
docker buildx create --use

# Build and push for multiple architectures
docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64,linux/arm/v7 -t your-registry/prometheus-speedtest-exporter:latest .

docs.title: Release Process
docs.text:
1. Update version in Cargo.toml
  2. Create and push a new tag: 
    git tag -a v0.2.3 -m "Release v0.2.3"
git push origin v0.2.3
  3. The GitHub Actions workflow will automatically:
  4. Create a GitHub release
  5. Build and upload binaries for all supported architectures
  6. Build and push Docker images
  7. Deploy documentation updates

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: The exporter provides the following Prometheus metrics:

docs.title: Speed Metrics
docs.text: Metric Description Type speedtest_download_bits_per_second Download speed in bits per second Gauge speedtest_upload_bits_per_second Upload speed in bits per second Gauge

docs.title: Latency Metrics
docs.text: Metric Description Type speedtest_ping_latency_milliseconds Ping latency in milliseconds Gauge speedtest_jitter_latency_milliseconds Jitter (latency variation) in milliseconds Gauge

docs.title: Server Information
docs.text: Metric Description Type speedtest_server_info Information about the speedtest server used Info speedtest_client_info Information about the client (ISP, location) Info

docs.title: Operational Metrics
docs.text: Metric Description Type speedtest_test_duration_seconds Duration of the speedtest in seconds Gauge speedtest_test_error Error status of the last test (1 = error, 0 = success) Gauge

docs.title: Example Metrics Output
docs.text:
# HELP speedtest_download_bits_per_second Download speed in bits per second
# TYPE speedtest_download_bits_per_second gauge
speedtest_download_bits_per_second 100000000

# HELP speedtest_upload_bits_per_second Upload speed in bits per second
# TYPE speedtest_upload_bits_per_second gauge
speedtest_upload_bits_per_second 50000000

# HELP speedtest_ping_latency_milliseconds Ping latency in milliseconds
# TYPE speedtest_ping_latency_milliseconds gauge
speedtest_ping_latency_milliseconds 15.5

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: The fastest way to get started is using our Docker Compose setup, which includes: - Speedtest exporter (runs every 30 minutes) - Prometheus (scrapes metrics every hour) - Grafana (with pre-configured dashboard)

docs.title: Using Docker Compose
docs.text:
1. Download our Docker Compose file: 

    curl -o docker-compose.yml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lpicanco/prometheus-speedtest-exporter/main/docker-compose.yml

  2. Start the stack: 

    docker-compose up -d

That's it! Your monitoring stack is now running: - Speedtest exporter: http://localhost:9516/metrics - Prometheus: http://localhost:9090 - Grafana: http://localhost:3000 (default credentials: admin/admin)

The Grafana dashboard will be automatically provisioned and ready to show your internet speed metrics.
